title: CHAPTER 1 : INTRODUCING PHILOSOPHY
content:
ሰላም ሰላም! ውድ የEthioFresh ቤተሰቦች፤ እንኳን ወደ Logic & Critical Thinking Chapter 1, Lesson 3 በሰላም መጣችሁ! ዛሬ ደግሞ የፊሎሶፊን ሁለት ዋና ዋና ዘርፎች ማለትም Metaphysics እና Epistemologyን በጥልቀት እንመረምራለን። ዶርም ውስጥ ተቀምጣችሁ "እውነት እኔ አሁን እዚህ አጠናለሁ ወይስ በሕልሜ ነው?" ብላችሁ ተጠይቃችሁ የምታውቁ ከሆነ—እንኳን ደስላችሁ፣ አስሬ Metaphysics እና Epistemology ውስጥ ገብታችኋል ማለት ነው! 😄 እስኪ ዛሬ ነገሩን ቀለል አድርገን ለፈተና 100% ዝግጁ እንሁን! 👇👇👇


Lesson 3: Metaphysics and Epistemology

Lesson Overview:
Philosophy is a rational and critical enterprise that tries to formulate and answer fundamental questions through an intensive application of reason—an application that draws on analysis, comparison, and evaluation. It deals with the most basic issues faced by human beings. The content of philosophy is better seen as asking the right questions rather than providing the correct answers. It can even be said that philosophy is the study of questions. Van Cleve Morris noted that the crux of the matter is asking the "right" questions—meaning questions that are meaningful and relevant, which will make a difference in how people live and work. Philosophy has primary and secondary branches. This course deals with the primary ones: Metaphysics, Epistemology, Axiology, and Logic.

Lesson Objectives:
After a successful completion of this lesson, you will be able to:
• Understand the fundamental concerns and issues that metaphysics and epistemology primarily deal with.
• Identify the major subsets or aspects of metaphysical questions.
• Recognize the fundamental philosophical (epistemological) debates concerning the sources of human knowledge.

👉 • ፊሎሶፊ ከምንም በላይ "ትክክለኛ ጥያቄዎችን የመጠየቅ ጥበብ" ነው! Van Cleve Morris እንደገለጸው፣ ዋናው ቁልፍ ነጥብ ትርጉም ያላቸውንና የሰዎችን ሕይወት የሚለውጡ ጥያቄዎችን መጠየቅ ነው። ፊሎሶፊ ዋና ዋና (Primary) እና ሁለተኛ ደረጃ (Secondary) ዘርፎች ያሉት ሲሆን፣ በዚህ ሌሰን ውስጥ የመጀመሪያዎቹን ሁለቱን—Metaphysics (ስለ እውነታ እና ህልውና የሚያጠና) እና Epistemology (ስለ እውቀት አመጣጥና ተፈጥሮ የሚያጠና)—በስፋት እናያለን።


3.1 Metaphysics

Metaphysics is the branch of philosophy that studies the ultimate nature of reality or existence. It deals with issues of reality, God, freedom, soul/immortality, the mind-body problem, form and substance relationship, cause and effect relationship, and other related issues. Metaphysicians seek an irreducible foundation of reality or 'first principles' from which absolute knowledge or truth can be induced and deduced.

Etymology: The term metaphysics is derived from the Greek words "meta" (meaning "beyond", "upon", or "after") and physika (meaning "physics"). Literally, it refers to "those things after the physics." Aristotle's writings on 'first philosophy' came after his treatise on physics; therefore, Aristotle's editor, Andronicus of Rhodes, named them metaphysics.

Questions Metaphysics deals with:
• What is reality?
• What is the ultimately real?
• What is the nature of the ultimate reality?
• Is it one thing or is it many different things?
• Can reality be grasped by the senses, or is it transcendent?
• What makes reality different from a mere appearance?
• What is mind, and what is its relation to the body?
• Is there a cause and effect relationship between reality and appearance?
• Does God exist, and if so, can we prove it?
• Are human actions free, or predetermined by a supernatural force?
• What is human being? A thinking mind? A perishable body? Or a combination of both?
• What is time?
• What is the meaning of life?

The Example of the Floor (George Knight):
Questions like "What is real?" seem too simple, but consider George Knight's example about a floor:
1. Common Sense View: The floor is flat, solid, smooth, brown, made of wood/concrete, and supports weight.
2. Physicist View: The floor is a dynamic structure of molecules, atoms, electrons, protons, neutrons, and pure electrical energy.
3. Chemist View: The floor is a complex combination of hydrocarbons subject to environmental conditions like heat, cold, oxidation, etc.

This illustrates that reality is not as simple as it appears on the surface.

👉 • Metaphysics ማለት ስለ እውነታ (Reality) ወይም ስለ ህልውና (Existence) የመጨረሻ ተፈጥሮ የሚያጠና የፊሎሶፊ ዘርፍ ነው። "Meta" ማለት "ከዚያ በላይ/በኋላ" ማለት ሲሆን "Physika" ማለት ደግሞ "ፊዚክስ/ቁሳዊ ነገር" ማለት ነው። ስለዚህ ከቁሳዊው ዓለም በላይ ያለውን እውነታ ይመረምራል።
👉 • ለምሳሌ የዶርማችሁን ወለል ብንወስድ፦ ተራ ሰው "ጠንካራና ጠፍጣፋ እንጨት ነው" ይላል፤ ፊዚሲስት ደግሞ "አይ፣ አተሞችና ኤሌክትሮኖች የሚንቀሳቀሱበት የኤነርጂ ስብስብ ነው" ይላል፤ ኬሚስቱ ደግሞ "የሃይድሮካርቦን ጥንቅር ነው" ይላል። አያችሁ አይደል? እውነታ (Reality) እኛ በምድራዊ ዓይናችን እንደምናየው ብቻ ቀላል አይደለም!

Subsets / Aspects of Metaphysics

Metaphysical questions are divided into four main subsets or aspects:

i) Cosmological Aspect: Cosmology is the study of theories about the origin, nature, and development of the universe as an orderly system. Questions include: "How did the universe originate and develop? Did it come about by accident or design? Does its existence have any purpose?"

ii) Theological Aspect: Theology is that part of religious theory that deals with conceptions of and about God. Questions include: "Is there a God? If so, is there one or more than one? What are the attributes of God? If God is all-good and all-powerful, why does evil exist? What is His relationship to human beings?"

iii) Anthropological Aspect: Anthropology (in metaphysics) deals with the study of human beings and asks questions like: "What is the relation between mind and body? Is mind more fundamental than body? What is humanity's moral status (born good, evil, or neutral)? Do humans have free will or are they determined? Does each person have a soul?"

iv) Ontological Aspect: Ontology is the study of the nature of existence, or what it means for anything to exist. Questions include: "Is basic reality found in matter/physical energy, or in spirit/spiritual energy? Is it composed of one element (monism), two (dualism), or many (pluralism)? Is reality fixed or constantly changing?"

👉 • Metaphysics አራት ዋና ዋና ክፍሎች አሉት፦
1. Cosmology: ስለ አጽናፈ ዓለም (Universe) አመጣጥና ምስረታ የሚያጠና።
2. Theology: ስለ አምላክ/ፈጣሪ ህልውና እና ባህሪያት የሚያጠና።
3. Anthropology: ስለ ሰው ልጅ ተፈጥሮ፣ የአእምሮና የአካል ግንኙነት (Mind-Body) እና ነፃ ፈቃድ (Free Will) የሚያጠና።
4. Ontology: ስለ ህልውና (Existence) ዋና መሠረት (ቁስ ወይስ መንፈስ?) የሚያጠና።

3.2 Epistemology

Epistemology is the branch of philosophy that studies the nature, scope, meaning, and possibility of knowledge. It deals with issues of knowledge, opinion, truth, falsity, reason, experience, and faith. Epistemology is also referred to as the "theory of knowledge".

Etymology: Derived from the Greek words episteme (meaning "knowledge" or "understanding") and logos (meaning "study of"). It seeks to answer basic questions such as "What is true?" and "How do we know?"

Key Issues in Epistemology:
• Skepticism: The position claiming that people cannot acquire reliable knowledge and that any search for truth is in vain (e.g., Gorgias asserted that nothing exists, and if it did, we could not know it).
• Agnosticism: A profession of ignorance, particularly in reference to the existence or nonexistence of God.
• Relativity vs. Absoluteness of Truth: Is truth relative (changing according to context/time) or absolute (eternally and universally true everywhere)?
• Objectivity vs. Subjectivity: Is knowledge independent of human perception (objective) or constructed by individual experience (subjective)?

👉 • Epistemology ማለት ስለ እውቀት ተፈጥሮ፣ ወሰን፣ እና የመገኘት እድል የሚያጠና ዘርፍ ነው። "Theory of Knowledge" በመባልም ይታወቃል። ዋና ጥያቄውም "እውነት ምንድን ነው?" እና "አንድን ነገር እንደምናውቅ በምን እናውቃለን?" የሚል ነው።
👉 • እዚህ ላይ Skepticism (ምንም ዓይነት እርግጠኛ እውቀት ማግኘት አይቻልም የሚል አስተሳሰብ) እና Agnosticism (የአምላክን ህልውና ማወቅ አንችልም የሚል አቋም) ይነሳሉ።


Sources of Human Knowledge

How do human beings acquire knowledge? Epistemology identifies five major sources:

1. Empiricism (Sense Experience):
Knowledge obtained through the five senses (sight, hearing, touch, smell, taste). Sensory knowing is immediate and forms the basis of much human knowledge.
• Limitation: Human senses can be incomplete and undependable/deceptive (e.g., a straight stick looking bent when submerged in water; visual illusions, fatigue, or illness distorting perception).

2. Rationalism (Reason):
The view that reasoning, thought, or logic is the central factor in knowledge. Rationalists claim that senses only provide raw, disorganized materials; the mind must organize them into meaningful knowledge. Formal logic is a major tool for rationalists.
• Advantage: Internal consistency and certainty.
• Limitation: Risk of being disconnected from external physical reality if premises are false.

3. Intuition:
The direct apprehension of knowledge without conscious reasoning or immediate sense perception. Experienced as a sudden flash of insight or an "immediate feeling of certainty".
• Advantage: Can bypass the limitations of human experience.
• Limitation: Unreliable when used alone; easily goes astray unless checked by reason or experience.

4. Revelation:
Knowledge communicated by a transcendent, supernatural reality (God) breaking into the natural order. Central to religious beliefs (e.g., God's communication of divine will).
• Advantage: Considered by believers as an omniscient, absolute, and uncontaminated source.
• Limitation: Must be accepted by faith; cannot be proved or disproved empirically, and human interpretation can distort it.

5. Authority:
Knowledge accepted as true because it comes from experts, textbooks, teachers, or traditions.
• Advantage: Essential for society; civilization would stagnate if everyone had to personally verify everything firsthand.
• Limitation: If the authority is based on incorrect assumptions, the knowledge becomes distorted.

👉 • የአምስቱ የእውቀት ምንጮች ማጠቃለያ፦
• Empiricism: በስሜት ህዋሳት (Senses) የሚገኝ እውቀት። (ግን አንዳንዴ ስሜት ህዋሳታችን ይሸውዱናል—ለምሳሌ ውኃ ውስጥ የተነከረ እንጨት ተጠምዝዞ መታየቱ!)
• Rationalism: በአእምሮ አስተስሰቦ እና በLogic የሚገኝ እውቀት።
• Intuition: ድንገተኛ ውስጣዊ ስሜት/ግንዛቤ (Flash of insight)።
• Revelation: ከፈጣሪ በራዕይ/በወረደ ቃል የሚገኝ መንፈሳዊ እውቀት።
• Authority: ከአስተማሪዎች፣ ከመጻሕፍት ወይም ከባለሙያዎች የተቀበልነው እውቀት።

💡 Exam Hint: በፈተናዎች ላይ "Stick submerged in water looks bent" የሚለው ምሳሌ ሲመጣ መልሱ Empiricism / Limitation of Sense Perception ነው! እንዲሁም "Reason is the primary source of knowledge" ከተባለ Rationalism ነው! እነዚህን አምስት ምንጮች በደንብ ለዩአቸው!


የክፍሉ ማጠቃለያ ጥያቄዎች (Exam-Style Questions)

1. Which branch of metaphysics studies the origin, nature, and development of the universe as an orderly system?
A) Ontology
B) Theology
C) Cosmology
D) Anthropology
Answer: C
Explanation: Cosmology is specifically concerned with the origin and structure of the universe (cosmos).

2. A student argues that "We cannot trust our sight completely because an oar submerged in water appears broken." This limitation directly challenges which source of knowledge?
A) Rationalism
B) Empiricism
C) Revelation
D) Intuition
Answer: B
Explanation: Empiricism relies on sensory perception. The bent stick in water illustrates the deceptive nature of senses.

3. The word "Metaphysics" literally translates to:
A) Theory of Knowledge
B) Study of Values
C) Those things after the physics
D) Study of logical reasoning
Answer: C
Explanation: From Greek "meta" (after/beyond) and "physika" (physics), coined when Andronicus of Rhodes arranged Aristotle's works after his treatise on physics.
